verdict: Lend selectively in Sangli sugar and ethanol — pursue integrated mills with distillery capacity and tied cane, avoid pure-standalone crushers and unhedged greenfield distillery capex; the local signal is mixed, so structure tightly and take monthly data.
title: Sangli Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Sangli mill buys cane from member and non-member farmers, crushes it into sugar, molasses and bagasse, and increasingly diverts juice or molasses into ethanol. Cash arrives in two lumps: sugar sold through releases and ethanol sold to OMCs on tender. **The whole model is a working-capital cycle, not a fixed-asset story** — cane is paid within days of crushing while sugar and ethanol receivables come back over months. ## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in recovery rate and in the ethanol diversion, not in the sugar price alone. **Integrated mills with distillery capacity earn a second, contracted margin that pure crushers do not have** — ICRA notes remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention for debt-funded distillery capex are what keep cane arrears from piling up [10]. Peer evidence supports the split: Triveni's Q1 FY27 profitability came from sugar and distillery margins with reduced debt [5], and EID Parry's realisation moved to INR 51.2 per kg from INR 43.7 per kg on premium mix [6]. ## What has changed now
Maharashtra's GST collections are running +8.6% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D] — a genuine local tailwind. But Maharashtra electricity demand is +6.0% against India's +9.5% [D], a 3.5 pp lag that says industrial activity in the state is softer than the national picture. Nationally, bank credit is -7.0% YoY against output +5.1% [D]. **The data call is OK at 66, but the local stress signal and the credit-output gap mean you lend to the strong and decline the marginal.** Note the local political noise around the G.D. Bapu successors [1] is a governance signal on cooperative mills, not a credit number — treat it as a reason to read the board resolution and cane-payment record, not as a figure. ## Who to pursue, who to avoid
Pursue integrated mills with own distillery, tied cane area and a clean cane-arrears record; pursue ethanol-only capex where the OMC offtake letter is in hand. Avoid standalone crushers with no ethanol outlet, mills with unpaid cane arrears, and greenfield distillery capex funded largely by debt. **Take monthly cane-crushing and cane-payment statements, quarterly stock-and-receivable statements, and the OMC contract copy at sanction.** Structure as a cash-flow loan against release orders with a receivables charge, and covenant a maximum cane-arrears days figure — collect from customer, since no source gives a Sangli-specific number. ## Early-warning signs
- Cane arrears days rising month-on-month (monthly) -> stop fresh disbursement and ask for the farmer payment schedule. - Sugar recovery rate falling below the mill's own prior-season figure (seasonal) -> re-rate the proposal and cut drawing power. - Ethanol offtake letter not renewed or OMC tender lost (quarterly) -> shift the facility to a sugar-only structure or decline. - Stock-to-sales rising while releases stay flat (quarterly) -> ask for the release-order book and inspect godown stock.
watch: above the mill's own prior-season peak -> freeze disbursement and demand farmer payment proof
below prior season -> cut drawing power and re-price
lapsed or tender lost -> convert to sugar-only structure or decline
stock-to-sales rising with flat releases -> inspect godown and ask for release book
continues below India -> tighten new-to-bank cooperative mill limits
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local crush plans current and real; state GST strong but power demand lags, so mixed.
